DILG • BAGONG PIUPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dil . ov. h OILG OPINION NO. AUG 06 2025 HON. ROWENA R. TUASON Vice Mayor City of Masbate Dear Vice Mayor Tuason: This pertains to your letter dated February 12, 2025 requesting for legal opinion on the interpretation and application of Section 323 of the Local Government Code, particularly on whether the Sangguniang Panlungsod may include other urgent matters in its sessions while the annual budget for Fiscal Year 2025 remains pending approval. As noted in your letter, the Local Chief Executive of Masbate City submitted the proposed Annual Budget for Fiscal Year 2025 in September 2024. However, as of the submission of this query, the Sangguniang Panlungsod has yet to approve the same, and it remains under committee consideration. Consequently, since January 2025, the Sanggunian has been holding sessions with the annual budget as the sole item in the order of business, pursuant to Section 323 of the LGC. Concerns have been raised about the recurring failure to act on the budget, reportedly due to persistent absenteeism and procedural tactics leading to repeated adjournments. In light of this, your office has sought clarification on whether other urgent matters — including the approval of barangay budgets, authority for the City Mayor to enter into various Memoranda of Agreement (MOAS), and the reading of minutes of special sessions may be taken up during such sessions. Further clarification is also sought on whether the Committee of the Whole may conduct hearings either during regular sessions or on non-session days for further evaluation of the proposed budget. After careful review, we provide the foregoing discussion and opinion: Section 323 of the LGC is unequivocal that if the sanggunian fails to pass the annual appropriations ordinance at the beginning of the fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, "without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions." The said provision aims to emphasize urgency and legislative priority that the Sanggunian must uphold in enacting the annual budget, as it is essential to ensure uninterrupted local government operations. DILG Opinion No. 20, series of 2014, reinforces this point, wherein the Department asserted that "[t]he first sentence of Section 323 of the Code needs no further elucidation as it clearly states that if the SB fails to pass an ordinance authorizing the annual budget, it shall continue to hold sessions, until such ordinance is approved and no other business may be taken up during such sessions."l I Issued on June 3, 2014. See also DILG Opinion No. 3, series of 2013 issued on January 24, 2013. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

A similar position of the Department is expressed in DILG Opinion No. 108, series of 2021 , which states that: "The rationale for the rule that 'no other business may be taken up during (said) sessions" can be found in Section 308 of the LGC, that is, unless and until the Appropriations Ordinance is approved, no money shall be paid out of the local treasury. Therefore, the Appropriations Ordinance is the most important piece of legislation in a local government unit. The prohibition on taking up other businesses during sanggunian sessions is intended to compel the sanggunian members to devote all their attention to the enactment of the Appropriation Ordinance."2 In this regard, it is our considered view that the Sanggunian cannot validly include or deliberate upon any other item in its order of business the approval of barangay budgets or authorizing the City Mayor to enter into various MOAs during sessions convened for the purpose of passing the annual budget. Such matters, regardless of their importance or urgency, must be deferred until the annual budget is approved or addressed in a legally distinct special session that does not contravene the intent of Section 323. With respect to your second query regarding the reading and consideration of the minutes Of special sessions, these too are considered business under the Sanggunian's order of business. Therefore, they cannot be included in sessions exclusively devoted to the pending annual budget. Once the budget is approved, the minutes may be duly included for reading and approval in the succeeding or subsequent regular session or in a dedicated special session convened for that purpose. To reiterate, the law affords no exception based on urgency or relevance; the legislative intent is clear in mandating singular focus on the annual appropriations ordinance. Concerning the recommitment of the proposed annual budget to the Committee of the Whole, the Department posits that it is within the Sanggunian's prerogative to refer the proposed budget to this body for further study and deliberation. The Committee of the Whole may conduct hearings either during a regular session or on other days, provided that such meetings are solely focused on the proposed budget and do not include unrelated matters. This procedure is consistent with legislative practice and does not violate Section 323, so long as the deliberations remain strictly limited to the annual appropriations ordinance. In conclusion, Section 323 mandates a focused and uninterrupted consideration of the annual budget, and as such, does not permit the inclusion of unrelated legislative or administrative matters during the pendency of its approval. Compliance with this provision is important not only for legal propriety but also for the timely and effective operation of the local government. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. 2 Issued on August 25, 2021. Page 2 of 3

We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P.
